Building on data-free parameter pruning, which systematically removes redundant neurons, and Deep Roots, which exploits sparse inter-layer dependencies to reduce computational cost, we propose a unified framework that integrates these techniques with wide residual networks to achieve superior accuracy and efficiency. Our method enables significant parameter reduction, up to 85% in some cases, while maintaining or improving performance on benchmark datasets such as CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and COCO. Additionally, we incorporate learned group convolutions and dynamic network surgery to further enhance efficiency without compromising accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance with reduced computational complexity, making it highly suitable for deployment on resource-constrained platforms.

original_abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of generating a set ofrealistic and diverse backgrounds when given only a smallforeground region. We refer to this task as image outpaint-ing. The technical challenge of this task is to synthesize notonly plausible but also diverse image outputs. Traditionalgenerative adversarial networks suffer from mode collapse.While recent approaches propose to maximize orpreserve the pairwise distance between generated sampleswith respect to their latent distance, they do not explicitlyprevent the diverse samples of different conditional inputsfrom collapsing. Therefore, we propose a new regulariza-tion method to encourage diverse sampling in conditionalsynthesis. In addition, we propose a feature pyramid dis-criminator to improve the image quality. Our experimen-tal results show that our model can produce more diverseimages without sacrificing visual quality compared to state-of-the-arts approaches in both the CelebA face dataset and the Cityscape scene dataset.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines context-aware feature learning, adversarial training, and probabilistic synthesis for advanced image generation and inpainting tasks. Building on context encoders, adversarial feature learning, and generative models with contextual attention, our approach leverages deep perceptual features and bidirectional generative networks to synthesize realistic and semantically coherent image content. By integrating probabilistic future frame synthesis with cross-convolutional networks and edge-aware inpainting strategies, we achieve high-quality image completion and generation that preserves both structural and textural details. Additionally, our method supports diverse applications such as scene composition, text-to-image synthesis, and object insertion, demonstrating superior performance across multiple benchmarks through enhanced perceptual similarity and semantic consistency.

original_abstract: Neural machine translation (NMT) is one of the best methods for understanding the differences in semantic rules between two languages. Especially for Indo-European languages, subword-level models have achieved impressive results. However, when the translation task involves Chinese, semantic granularity remains at the word and character level, so there is still need more fine-grained translation model of Chinese. In this paper, we introduce a simple and effective method for Chinese translation at the sub-character level. Our approach uses the Wubi method to translate Chinese into English; byte-pair encoding (BPE) is then applied. Our method for Chinese-English translation eliminates the need for a complicated word segmentation algorithm during preprocessing. Furthermore, our method allows for sub-character-level neural translation based on recurrent neural network (RNN) architecture, without preprocessing. The empirical results show that for Chinese-English translation tasks, our sub-character-level model has a comparable BLEU score to the subword model, despite having a much smaller vocabulary. Additionally, the small vocabulary is highly advantageous for NMT model compression.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel hybrid neural machine translation (NMT) framework that combines the strengths of subword, character-level, and word-level modeling to achieve robust open-vocabulary translation across diverse language pairs. Building on prior work that leverages subword units for handling rare and unknown words, character-level models for eliminating segmentation dependencies, and hybrid architectures for balancing efficiency and accuracy, our approach integrates these techniques into a unified system. The model employs a subword encoder for standard vocabulary items, a character-level decoder for generating unseen word forms, and an attention mechanism to dynamically align source and target segments. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this hybrid system on multiple WMT'15 language pairs, achieving significant improvements in BLEU scores compared to word-based and subword-based baselines. Additionally, the model exhibits strong performance on morphologically rich and structurally dissimilar language pairs, such as Chinese-English, through the use of ASCII-based encoding schemes. Our results highlight the potential of combining subword and character-level representations with attention-based alignment to enhance both the flexibility and accuracy of NMT systems in open-vocabulary scenarios.

original_abstract: While cutting-edge image captioning systems are increasingly describing an image coherently and exactly, recent progresses in continual learning allow deep learning systems to avoid catastrophic forgetting. However, the domain where image captioning working with continual learning is not exploited yet. We define the task in which we consolidate continual learning and image captioning as continual image captioning. In this work, we propose ContCap, a framework continually generating captions over a series of new tasks coming, seamlessly integrating continual learning into image captioning accompanied by tackling catastrophic forgetting. After proving catastrophic forgetting in image captioning, we employ freezing, knowledge distillation, and pseudo-labeling techniques to overcome the forgetting dilemma with the baseline is a simple fine-tuning scheme. We split MS-COCO 2014 dataset to perform experiments on incremental tasks without revisiting dataset of previously provided tasks. The experiments are designed to increase the degree of catastrophic forgetting and appraise the capacity of approaches. Experimental results show remarkable improvements in the performance on the old tasks, while the figure for the new task remains almost the same compared to fine-tuning. For example, pseudo-labeling increases CIDEr from 0.287 to 0.576 on the old task and 0.686 down to 0.657 BLEU1 on the new task.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for continual learning in semantic segmentation, combining progressive neural networks with incremental classifier learning strategies to address catastrophic forgetting. By integrating knowledge distillation from previous models and leveraging a distillation loss that balances old and new class information, the approach enables the network to learn new classes without access to original training data. The method also incorporates generative adversarial networks to synthesize representative exemplars for old classes, mitigating privacy concerns and improving generalization. Experimental results on the Pascal VOC2012 and COCO datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in incremental semantic segmentation, maintaining high accuracy on previously learned classes while effectively adapting to new ones.

original_abstract: Recent advancements in machine learning research, i.e., deep learning, introduced methods that excel conventional algorithms as well as humans in several complex tasks, ranging from detection of objects in images and speech recognition to playing difficult strategic games. However, the current methodology of machine learning research and consequently, implementations of the real-world applications of such algorithms, seems to have a recurring HARKing (Hypothesizing After the Results are Known) issue. In this work, we elaborate on the algorithmic, economic and social reasons and consequences of this phenomenon. We present examples from current common practices of conducting machine learning research (e.g. avoidance of reporting negative results) and failure of generalization ability of the proposed algorithms and datasets in actual real-life usage. Furthermore, a potential future trajectory of machine learning research and development from the perspective of accountable, unbiased, ethical and privacy-aware algorithmic decision making is discussed. We would like to emphasize that with this discussion we neither claim to provide an exhaustive argumentation nor blame any specific institution or individual on the raised issues. This is simply a discussion put forth by us, insiders of the machine learning field, reflecting on us.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework that combines reinforcement learning, evolutionary strategies, and random search to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of neural architecture search (NAS). By integrating sequential model-based optimization with regularized evolution, we propose a method that systematically explores architectural spaces while maintaining computational efficiency. Our approach leverages transferable building blocks and incorporates early-stopping and weight-sharing mechanisms to improve search performance and reproducibility. Experimental results on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while reducing computational costs compared to existing NAS techniques. Furthermore, we address the generalization concerns of current models by evaluating performance on newly created test sets, showing improved robustness to distribution shifts. This work provides a comprehensive evaluation of the search phase, emphasizing the importance of search strategy quality in discovering superior architectures.

original_abstract: One of the primary challenges faced by deep learning is the degree to which current methods exploit superficial statistics and dataset bias, rather than learning to generalise over the specific representations they have experienced. This is a critical concern because generalisation enables robust reasoning over unseen data, whereas leveraging superficial statistics is fragile to even small changes in data distribution. To illuminate the issue and drive progress towards a solution, we propose a test that explicitly evaluates abstract reasoning over visual data. We introduce a large-scale benchmark of visual questions that involve operations fundamental to many high-level vision tasks, such as comparisons of counts and logical operations on complex visual properties. The benchmark directly measures a method's ability to infer high-level relationships and to generalise them over image-based concepts. It includes multiple training/test splits that require controlled levels of generalization. We evaluate a range of deep learning architectures, and find that existing models, including those popular for vision-and-language tasks, are unable to solve seemingly-simple instances. Models using relational networks fare better but leave substantial room for improvement.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for Visual Question Answering (VQA) that integrates structured representations, zero-shot reasoning, and meta-learning capabilities. Building on recent advances in graph-based scene and question modeling, we propose a system that captures the structural complexity of both visual and linguistic inputs through graph neural networks. To address the limitations of traditional VQA models in handling unseen concepts, we incorporate zero-shot learning strategies, including semantic embeddings and test-time retrieval, enabling the model to answer questions about previously unseen images and novel question types. Furthermore, we treat VQA as a meta-learning task, allowing the model to dynamically utilize a support set of examples at test time to generate accurate and novel answers. Our approach demonstrates significant improvements in accuracy across multiple benchmarks, including the "abstract scenes" and "balanced scenes" datasets, while also achieving state-of-the-art performance in zero-shot and meta-learning settings. The proposed framework represents a step toward more flexible, generalizable, and reasoning-capable vision-and-language systems.

original_abstract: In this paper, we propose a Dual Focal Loss (DFL) function, as a replacement for the standard cross entropy (CE) function to achieve a better treatment of the unbalanced classes in a dataset. Our DFL method is an improvement on the recently reported Focal Loss (FL) cross-entropy function, which proposes a scaling method that puts more weight on the examples that are difficult to classify over those that are easy. However, the scaling parameter of FL is empirically set, which is problem-dependent. In addition, like other CE variants, FL only focuses on the loss of true classes. Therefore, no loss feedback is gained from the false classes. Although focusing only on true examples increases probability on true classes and correspondingly reduces probability on false classes due to the nature of the softmax function, it does not achieve the best convergence due to avoidance of the loss on false classes. Our DFL method improves on the simple FL in two ways. Firstly, it takes the idea of FL to focus more on difficult examples than the easy ones, but evaluates loss on both true and negative classes with equal importance. Secondly, the scaling parameter of DFL has been made learnable so that it can tune itself by backpropagation rather than being dependent on manual tuning. In this way, our proposed DFL method offers an auto-tunable loss function that can reduce the class imbalance effect as well as put more focus on both true difficult examples and negative easy examples. Experimental results show that our proposed method provides better accuracy in every test run conducted over a variety of different network models and datasets.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel deep learning framework for brain tumor segmentation that integrates advanced encoder-decoder architectures with hierarchical loss functions and efficient convolutional strategies. Building on fully convolutional networks (FCNs), we incorporate atrous separable convolutions and dilated convolutions to enhance contextual understanding while reducing computational complexity. A refined hierarchical dice loss is introduced to address class imbalance, inspired by the hierarchical relationships between tumor subtypes. Additionally, we adopt a cascaded CNN structure and a two-phase training procedure to improve segmentation accuracy and robustness. The proposed model combines the strengths of DeepLabv3+ and U-Net architectures, leveraging skip connections and multi-scale feature fusion for precise localization. Experimental results on the BRATS dataset demonstrate significant improvements in segmentation performance, with a mean Dice score of 89.4% and a 40-fold speed increase over existing methods, establishing a new benchmark for efficient and accurate brain tumor segmentation.

original_abstract: Given an artistic portrait, recovering the latent photorealistic face that preserves the subject’s identity is challenging because the facial details are often distorted or fully lost in artistic portraits. We develop an Identity-preserving Face Recovery from Portraits method that utilizes a Style Removal network (SRN) and a Discriminative Network (DN). Our SRN, composed of an autoencoder with residual block-embedded skip connections, is designed to transfer feature maps of stylized images to the feature maps of the corresponding photorealistic faces. Owing to the Spatial Transformer Network, SRN automatically compensates for misalignments of stylized portraits to output aligned realistic face images. To ensure the identity preservation, we promote the recovered and ground truth faces to share similar visual features via a distance measure which compares features of recovered and ground truth faces extracted from a pre-trained FaceNet network. DN has multiple convolutional and fully-connected layers, and its role is to enforce recovered faces to be similar to authentic faces. Thus, we can recover high-quality photorealistic faces from unaligned portraits while preserving the identity of the face in an image. By conducting extensive evaluations on a large-scale synthesized dataset and a hand-drawn sketch dataset, we demonstrate that our method achieves superior face recovery and attains state-of-the-art results. In addition, our method can recover photorealistic faces from unseen stylized portraits, artistic paintings, and hand-drawn sketches.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for content-aware, real-time arbitrary style transfer that combines the strengths of perceptual loss functions, adaptive instance normalization, and multiscale texture synthesis. By integrating histogram losses and localized style controls, our approach enhances texture quality, stability, and user controllability while maintaining efficiency. The method leverages a learned representation of artistic style to enable flexible style interpolation and combination from multiple sources. Furthermore, we employ a feed-forward network trained with perceptual losses to achieve high-quality stylization at speeds comparable to existing methods, without restricting the set of applicable styles. The proposed framework demonstrates improved convergence, visual quality, and artistic control over previous approaches, enabling diverse and controllable stylization of arbitrary content and style images.

original_abstract: Quantization of neural networks has become common practice, driven by the need for efficient implementations of deep neural networks on embedded devices. In this paper, we exploit an oft-overlooked degree of freedom in most networks - for a given layer, individual output channels can be scaled by any factor provided that the corresponding weights of the next layer are inversely scaled. Therefore, a given network has many factorizations which change the weights of the network without changing its function. We present a conceptually simple and easy to implement method that uses this property and show that proper factorizations significantly decrease the degradation caused by quantization. We show improvement on a wide variety of networks and achieve state-of-the-art degradation results for MobileNets. While our focus is on quantization, this type of factorization is applicable to other domains such as network-pruning, neural nets regularization and network interpretability.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for efficient deep neural network (DNN) deployment on embedded systems by combining low-precision quantization, network compression, and optimized training strategies. Building on recent advances in quantization techniques, including stochastic rounding, incremental network quantization (INQ), and analytical clipping, we propose a unified approach that enables training and inference with as few as 2-bit precision while maintaining high classification accuracy on ImageNet. Our method integrates pruning, per-channel weight quantization, and quantization-aware training to reduce model size by up to 49x and improve energy efficiency by 3x to 7x compared to full-precision baselines. Additionally, we demonstrate that with proper activation range calibration and gradient noise mitigation, low-precision networks can closely approximate full-precision models without requiring extensive retraining. The proposed framework is validated across multiple architectures, including ResNet, VGG, and MobileNet, and is shown to be compatible with both general-purpose and specialized hardware accelerators.

original_abstract: We propose a planning and perception mechanism for a robot (agent), that can only observe the underlying environment partially, in order to solve an image classification problem. A three-layer architecture is suggested that consists of a meta-layer that decides the intermediate goals, an action-layer that selects local actions as the agent navigates towards a goal, and a classification-layer that evaluates the reward and makes a prediction. We design and implement these layers using deep reinforcement learning. A generalized policy gradient algorithm is utilized to learn the parameters of these layers to maximize the expected reward. Our proposed methodology is tested on the MNIST dataset of handwritten digits, which provides us with a level of explainability while interpreting the agent's intermediate goals and course of action.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel deep learning framework that integrates the strengths of Network In Network (NIN), Dense Convolutional Networks (DenseNet), and multi-agent reinforcement learning to address complex image classification and autonomous decision-making tasks. By combining micro neural networks with dense connectivity, the proposed architecture enhances local feature abstraction and global information flow, leading to improved model discriminability and efficiency. Furthermore, we incorporate multi-agent reinforcement learning to enable decentralized, collaborative image classification, where agents exchange information and update beliefs through a consensus protocol. The framework is evaluated on benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior performance in both classification accuracy and adaptability in dynamic environments.

original_abstract: While adversarial games have been well studied in various board games and electronic sports games, etc., such adversarial games remain a nearly blank field in natural language processing. As natural language is inherently an interactive game, we propose a challenging pragmatics game called Adversarial Taboo, in which an attacker and a defender compete with each other through sequential natural language interactions. The attacker is tasked with inducing the defender to speak a target word invisible to the defender, while the defender is tasked with detecting the target word before being induced by the attacker. In Adversarial Taboo, a successful attacker must hide its intention and subtly induce the defender, while a competitive defender must be cautious with its utterances and infer the intention of the attacker. To instantiate the game, we create a game environment and a competition platform. Sufficient pilot experiments and empirical studies on several baseline attack and defense strategies show promising and interesting results. Based on the analysis on the game and experiments, we discuss multiple promising directions for future research.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel end-to-end dialogue system that integrates generative hierarchical neural networks, diversity-promoting objective functions, pragmatic reasoning, and reinforcement learning to enhance the quality and naturalness of conversational responses. By extending hierarchical recurrent encoder-decoder models with Maximum Mutual Information (MMI) as the objective function, we address the tendency of neural models to generate generic responses, promoting diversity and relevance. The model incorporates pragmatic reasoning through neural listener-speaker architectures, enabling agents to infer and respond to the partner's intent. Additionally, deep reinforcement learning is applied to simulate long-term dialogue outcomes, encouraging informative, coherent, and engaging interactions. The system is evaluated on both automatic metrics and human judgments, demonstrating significant improvements in response quality, diversity, and task-oriented performance. The approach is further validated in collaborative and negotiation scenarios, where agents must strategically communicate using dynamic knowledge representations and planning mechanisms. This work represents a unified framework for building flexible, human-like dialogue systems capable of handling a wide range of conversational tasks.

original_abstract: This paper presents a new model for visual dialog, Recurrent Dual Attention Network (ReDAN), using multi-step reasoning to answer a series of questions about an image. In each question-answering turn of a dialog, ReDAN infers the answer progressively through multiple reasoning steps. In each step of the reasoning process, the semantic representation of the question is updated based on the image and the previous dialog history, and the recurrently-refined representation is used for further reasoning in the subsequent step. On the VisDial v1.0 dataset, the proposed ReDAN model achieves a new state-of-the-art of 64.47% NDCG score. Visualization on the reasoning process further demonstrates that ReDAN can locate context-relevant visual and textual clues via iterative refinement, which can lead to the correct answer step-by-step.
generated_abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for visual dialog that integrates stacked attention networks, dual attention mechanisms, and adversarial learning to address the challenges of multi-turn question answering, visual reference resolution, and natural language generation. By combining semantic question representation with multi-layer attention for progressive reasoning, associative attention memory for resolving interdependent references, and a synergistic image-question-answer network for precise answer selection, the proposed model enhances both discriminative and generative capabilities in visual dialog. Additionally, adversarial learning is employed to refine answer generation, ensuring human-like responses supported by interpretable reasoning. Extensive experiments on the Visual Dialog dataset demonstrate significant improvements in performance metrics, achieving state-of-the-art results in both answer accuracy and dialog fluency.

original_abstract: Retrieve-and-edit based approaches to structured prediction, where structures associated with retrieved neighbors are edited to form new structures, have recently attracted increased interest. However, much recent work merely conditions on retrieved structures (e.g., in a sequence-to-sequence framework), rather than explicitly manipulating them. We show we can perform accurate sequence labeling by explicitly (and only) copying labels from retrieved neighbors. Moreover, because this copying is label-agnostic, we can achieve impressive performance in zero-shot sequence-labeling tasks. We additionally consider a dynamic programming approach to sequence labeling in the presence of retrieved neighbors, which allows for controlling the number of distinct (copied) segments used to form a prediction, and leads to both more interpretable and accurate predictions.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel end-to-end sequence labeling framework that integrates advanced neural architectures and transfer learning strategies to enhance performance across multiple natural language processing tasks. Building on bidirectional LSTM-CNN-CRF models, we incorporate deep contextualized word representations and attention mechanisms inspired by the Transformer architecture to capture both syntactic and semantic features effectively. Additionally, we explore cross-task and cross-lingual transfer learning, leveraging pre-trained models such as BERT and FLORS to improve performance on low-resource and domain-specific tasks. Our approach eliminates the need for extensive feature engineering and manual data preprocessing, enabling robust performance on part-of-speech tagging, named entity recognition, and cross-lingual NER tasks. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in accuracy and F1 scores across multiple benchmark datasets, including state-of-the-art results on the CoNLL 2003 NER corpus and enhanced performance in Chinese social media NER through joint training of segmentation and recognition models.

original_abstract: We present a comprehensive analysis of how and why face recognition accuracy differs between men and women. We show that accuracy is lower for women due to the combination of (1) the impostor distribution for women having a skew toward higher similarity scores, and (2) the genuine distribution for women having a skew toward lower similarity scores. We show that this phenomenon of the impostor and genuine distributions for women shifting closer towards each other is general across datasets of African-American, Caucasian, and Asian faces. We show that the distribution of facial expressions may differ between male/female, but that the accuracy difference persists for image subsets rated confidently as neutral expression. The accuracy difference also persists for image subsets rated as close to zero pitch angle. Even when removing images with forehead partially occluded by hair/hat, the same impostor/genuine accuracy difference persists. We show that the female genuine distribution improves when only female images without facial cosmetics are used, but that the female impostor distribution also degrades at the same time. Lastly, we show that the accuracy difference persists even if a state-of-the-art deep learning method is trained from scratch using training data explicitly balanced between male and female images and subjects.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel deep face recognition framework that integrates advanced loss functions with large-scale, diverse face datasets to enhance performance across challenging covariates such as age, pose, and illumination. Building on the angular softmax (A-Softmax) loss, additive angular margin loss (ArcFace), and large margin cosine loss (CosFace), we propose a unified loss function that combines the geometric discriminative power of angular margins with the normalization benefits of cosine loss, enabling more effective feature discrimination. The framework is evaluated on the VGGFace2 and MS-Celeb-1M datasets, which provide extensive variations in age, pose, and ethnicity, and is further tested on multiple face recognition benchmarks including IJB-A, IJB-B, and IJB-C. Our approach demonstrates superior performance over existing methods, particularly in handling age-related degradation in recognition accuracy, and achieves state-of-the-art results while maintaining computational efficiency. Additionally, we incorporate covariate-aware data curation strategies to improve model robustness, demonstrating that leveraging gender and age information during training can enhance verification performance at low false acceptance rates.

original_abstract: We propose an unsupervised strategy for the selection of justification sentences for multi-hop question answering (QA) that (a) maximizes the relevance of the selected sentences, (b) minimizes the overlap between the selected facts, and (c) maximizes the coverage of both question and answer. This unsupervised sentence selection method can be coupled with any supervised QA approach. We show that the sentences selected by our method improve the performance of a state-of-the-art supervised QA model on two multi-hop QA datasets: AI2's Reasoning Challenge (ARC) and Multi-Sentence Reading Comprehension (MultiRC). We obtain new state-of-the-art performance on both datasets among approaches that do not use external resources for training the QA system: 56.82\% F1 on ARC (41.24\% on Challenge and 64.49\% on Easy) and 26.1\% EM0 on MultiRC. Our justification sentences have higher quality than the justifications selected by a strong information retrieval baseline, e.g., by 5.4\% F1 in MultiRC. We also show that our unsupervised selection of justification sentences is more stable across domains than a state-of-the-art supervised sentence selection method.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for open-domain question answering that integrates multi-hop reasoning, evidence aggregation, and cross-document verification to address complex queries requiring information from multiple sources. Building on prior work in multi-passage reading comprehension, multi-hop inference, and answer re-ranking, our approach combines a graph-based reasoning model with an evidence aggregation mechanism to enhance answer accuracy and robustness. The system first retrieves relevant documents, then employs a graph convolutional network to model relationships between entities across passages, enabling multi-step reasoning. An answer re-ranking module leverages aggregated evidence through strength- and coverage-based strategies to refine candidate answers. Evaluated on benchmark datasets including HotpotQA, MS-MARCO, and TriviaQA, our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, demonstrating significant improvements over existing models in handling complex, multi-source questions.
